svg.text: Phoenix — four layers, one engine, one shared AI runtime underneath
Guided recording (Act 1) → Semantic resolution (Act 2) → Vision fusion → Autonomous loop (Act 3, Beta) — layers 2-4 all call the same Ollama model
1. Guided layer (Act 1) — shipped
A human walks the flow once, live, in the browser.
capture/recorder.js records each tap/type/scroll as an
exact, deterministic selector (resource-id / accessibility-id).
generation/pipeline.js infers assertions from the real diff and
synthesizes a runnable WebDriver script.
No AI/model call at runtime — the only layer that doesn't touch Ollama.
2. Semantic layer (Act 2) — shipped, proven on hardware
A plain-language instruction ("tap the LOGIN button") replaces a
hand-authored selector. generation/semantic-act.js's
resolveSemanticAction() grounds the live accessibility tree into a
numbered element list and sends it to Ollama to pick one —
or say "unresolved," never guess.
engine/semantic-act-executor.js then acts live via the same
WebDriver calls the guided path uses, and diffs the screen
before/after to know what really happened.
Self-heal: a "No visible change" tap triggers one automatic retry,
excluding the dead element, before anything is reported — live, in-run.
3. Vision fusion — shipped, opt-in
Text alone is ambiguous on icon-only controls (an unlabeled
"Right Icon" that's actually Logout; two sibling buttons with
generic ids). When a screenshot is available, semantic-act.js
sends it alongside the numbered element list via Ollama's
multimodal `images` field (generation/llm.js) — the model
confirms its text-based match against what the screen actually
looks like. Omitted entirely for a text-only model — nothing breaks,
it just resolves on tree text alone, the same as before fusion existed.
4. Autonomous loop (Act 3) — Beta
engine/semantic-loop.js takes a goal in plain language instead of a
step list: read the snapshot → ask Ollama to decide the single next
action (or stop) → execute it through the same executor as layer 2
→ feed the resulting diff back in as context → repeat.
Stops explicitly on: goal reached, model asks to stop, an action
fails/can't resolve, or a hard step-count limit — never a silent
retry loop. Wired into run-batch-executions.js's "loop" mode today.
Hardens through real TestOps usage -- same evidence-fix loop as layers 1-2.
Shared AI runtime — one model, three callers
generation/llm.js's callOllamaJson() is the ONLY place any layer talks to a model — a self-hosted Ollama server (local today; frothAI's Ollama endpoint is a config
change, not a code change: PHOENIX_OLLAMA_HOST / PHOENIX_OLLAMA_MODEL). Layers 2-4 all call it; layer 1 (guided) never does. Every call can return "can't tell" rather than a guess.
What ties all four together — and the one gap none of them closes
Every layer reports honestly rather than guessing: "unresolved" beats a confident wrong click, every time, across all four. engine/auto-heal.js is where layer 1
and layer 2 meet — a guided script's recorded selector falls back to a fresh semantic resolution if it stops matching or starts matching the wrong element.
Known gap: "succeeded" means no step errored — it is not proof the real on-screen goal was reached. A step can click a real, functioning, WRONG element and
still report success (closed per-flow today only by hand-authored tapIfExists selectors). Closing this generally needs outcome verification, not yet built.
